gen-gf-swanky-and-moo-moo-work-sans: Relaxed and inviting, Swanky and Moo Moo writes its capitals barely taller than the lowercase, like a casual pen on paper. Work Sans steps in with a modern sans-serif body, its c tips held well apart and its strokes sturdy.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-fs-karma: Karma sets a trustworthy, classic tone in its text. Syne Tactile adds a broad-nibbed, expressive stroke that never curls shut, and the two sit close in height, so they feel like old acquaintances with different accents.
gen-gf-syne-tactile-fs-paquito: Paquito reads confident and approachable, with capitals barely above the lowercase. Syne Tactile is best at showy broad-nib strokes that stay open, while Paquito is best at friendly, short bursts rather than long paragraphs.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-rowan: Rowan reads literary and friendly, with generous openings in every curve and thin strokes about half the weight of the thick ones. And Tapestry's hand-drawn, relaxed lettering, with horizontals as heavy as verticals, makes the pair feel personal rather than polished.
gen-gf-tapestry-fs-synonym: Relaxed and personal, Tapestry looks hand-drawn, with horizontals as thick as its verticals. Synonym follows in a dependable sans of constant ink and open curves, so a longer stretch of text would feel comfortable.
gen-gf-tektur-gf-hepta-slab: Hepta Slab reads bookish and dignified, with open counters that let the white space in. Its words stretch out wide and moderate in height, while Tektur's outsized lowercase makes a longer passage feel like a conversation with a sturdy elder.
gen-gf-tilt-prism-fs-karma: Bold, blocky and drawn with one tip, Tilt Prism keeps every line the same weight. But Karma brings a restrained thick-thin rhythm and a trustworthy, classic voice, and it can take a bit more size than you'd expect.
gen-gf-tilt-prism-fs-paquito: Tilt Prism's tails and terminals are as thick as its main stems, which gives it a bold, drawn-with-one-tip look. Paquito's confident, approachable text rides close beside it.
gen-gf-trade-winds-fs-rowan: Trade Winds has moderate contrast, neither stark nor flat, and a commanding, bold presence. Rowan brings a literary, friendly text serif, though shrinking the heading or enlarging the body would blur the difference.
gen-gf-tulpen-one-fs-rowan: Tulpen One looks bent from a single length of wire, bold and tightly packed. It is best at striking, rope-strand headlines, while Rowan is best at soft, literary text with a gentle thick-thin rhythm.
